name: Tech Mahindra Ltd
title: Tech Mahindra Ltd - 532755 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Tech Mahindra exited FY26 with Q4 margin 13.8% (up 70bp QoQ) and FY27 EBIT target of 15% reiterated, but growth is still soft at 0.6% CC for FY26 with no hard numbers on volume or pricing.

triggers.label: Q4 deal wins USD 1,073m, up 35% YoY
triggers.quote: The deal wins for the quarter stand at 1,073 million, up 35% YoY, and reflects continued deal momentum.

triggers.label: Revenue YoY exit ~4.9% reported
triggers.quote: almost a 5% year-on-year on a reported basis in the most recent quarter

triggers.label: Industry growth 2-5% estimate, no firm FY27 number

achieving organic constant currency revenue growth above our peer group's average
our commitment to all of you is get to 30% for next year

summary.headline: Tech Mahindra Q4 FY26 revenue rose 2.4% cc YoY to USD 1,625M, with EBIT margin at 13.8% and FY27 targets of 15% EBIT reiterated.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was USD 1,625M, up 0.9% QoQ and 4.9% YoY reported (2.4% YoY constant currency), with operating margin up 70 bps QoQ to 13.8%. Full-year FY26 revenue was USD 6,385M (+0.6% cc) and operating margin expanded 290 bps to 12.6%. Deal wins for the year reached USD 3.79B (+42% YoY) and the company reiterated FY27 targets of above-peer-average organic cc growth and a 15% EBIT margin. The analyst day framed AI as a modernization opportunity and highlighted Orion, Helix and a new pricing model, but did not report a standalone AI revenue figure.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 growth 5.9% YoY led by aerospace and industrial process manufacturing; Q4 up 11.8% YoY but flat QoQ. US auto softness offset by European auto ramp-up.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: FY26 growth 3.7% YoY; Q4 up 8% QoQ, the strongest QoQ vertical. Focus on payments, asset and wealth management, insurance and core platforms.

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: FY26 growth 2.6% YoY; Q4 up 5.6% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, helped by Comviva seasonality. Comviva grew double digits for a second year.

segments.name: Retail, Travel, Transportation and Logistics
segments.commentary: FY26 growth 7.3% YoY, the fastest vertical for the year; Q4 up 6.2% YoY. Driven by logistics and e-commerce tailwinds.

segments.name: Hi-Tech
segments.commentary: FY26 decline of 2.7% YoY on semiconductor client restructuring; Q4 up 6.6% YoY and 2.5% QoQ, with stabilisation in H2.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: FY26 roughly flat YoY (-0.6% per the Q&A slides); Q4 up 4.7% YoY. Regulatory pressure in provider and life sciences limits discretionary spend.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Europe grew 8.9% YoY in FY26, aided by currency. Americas broadly flat, with Communications growing and US auto soft.

guidance_outlook: FY27 targets reiterated: organic cc revenue growth above the peer-group average and EBIT margin of 15%.
Management expects FY27 growth to exceed FY26 and to be at par with or slightly above peers; industry growth estimated at roughly 2%-4% or 3%-5%.
FY27 normalised effective tax rate in a similar range to earlier guidance.
Margin expansion in FY27 to come mainly from fixed-price project productivity (AI-led), with the gap between T&M and fixed-price margins at about 8%.
Same four strategic metrics retained for the next 12 months; ROCE target of 30% next year.
Will look at tuck-in acquisitions for capability, not large transformational M&A.
capex_capacity: Investment priority shifting toward AI: LLMs, platform ecosystem and people investments.
Investments in sales and marketing, verticals and leadership were supplemented through FY26.
Fresh hiring: about 6,000 freshers in FY25 and 900+ in FY26; a higher number is planned for FY27.
Pyramid: average tenure of about nine years; management intends to improve pyramid through fresher adds in fixed-price transformation programmes.
Portfolio company integration: 100% front- and mid-office integrated; four to five back-end integrations to complete in FY27.
demand_pricing: Deal wins: USD 1,073M in Q4 (+35% YoY); FY26 deal wins USD 3.79B (+42%), the highest in several years, including a five-year Orange Business partnership and a large telecom deal in the prior quarter.
Revenue growth from large-deal wins has trended from -1% to 0.3%, 1.3% and 2.4% cc YoY over the last four quarters.
Clients have not delayed large-deal signings despite the Claude releases; some are pushing for higher outer-year productivity.
Management is moving toward a new AI-native pricing model based on service tokens that blends human and digital labour.
AI-led productivity improvement measured at 7% in programmes, excluding other lean and optimisation gains.
Clients' GenAI infusion stands at 90-95% for top accounts; 95% of peak and prime accounts have some GenAI offering.
Top-account metrics: 29 clients over USD 50M (+4 YoY) and 66 over USD 20M (+7 YoY); NPS now claimed as industry-leading.
Competition: GCCs are expanding; the company partners with them in some areas and competes in others.

qa_highlights.question: How achievable is FY27 outperformance versus peers when peers guide to slowing growth, and what is industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an improving exit trajectory, deal conversion and existing book expansion for confidence. It estimated industry growth at roughly 2%-4% or 3%-5%, and noted some clients may make discretionary cuts.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY27 margin expansion is cost-led versus growth-led, and how do mega-deal margins compare with older vintages?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said the cost/growth split is revised through the year and plans rely less on growth. As-sold margins on the large deals are accretive at portfolio level, per the board review.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete with frontier model companies' agents, and how is it differentiated in BFSI and retail where its exposure is smaller?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul said Orion focuses on agent orchestration and interoperability across agents. Mohit said focus is on four BFSI sub-areas (payments, asset and wealth, insurance, core banking), with industry experts hired, and cited retail CPG as a strong performer.

qa_highlights.question: Have clients delayed decisions or pushed for price deflation after the February Claude releases?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said there was no significant delay in large-deal signings. Some clients asked for higher outer-year productivity, but this was not common.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin of safety in the FY27 growth assumptions given telecom client pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said growth is linked to industry growth, and that the company's telecom business spans over 100 operators, plus BPS, network services and Comviva, which reduces single-client dependence.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 growth rely on telecom mega deals, and how will the company diversify away from telecom?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said the portfolio is diversifying into aerospace and defence, BFSI and retail CPG, and that pipeline BFSI and manufacturing deals should add meaningfully as they ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between fixed-price and T&M, and how will surplus margin be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said the gap is about 8%. The fixed-price margin improvement is the main lever for next year. Priorities for surplus are AI investment and growth.

risks_watch: Telecom concentration: potential spending cuts or leadership changes at large telecom clients.
Discretionary cuts by clients and project cancellations could hit FY27 growth.
Pricing pressure as clients demand higher AI productivity pass-through in fixed-price deals.
Competition from GCCs and frontier AI model companies' agent offerings.
Healthcare and Hi-Tech remain weak on discretionary spend; US auto recovery is at risk from the Middle East conflict.
DSO at 89 days; watch working-capital and receivables reduction.
Management has not yet put a number on AI-related revenue; promised to report a credible AI revenue metric in coming quarters.
Lumpy large-deal flow; the company warned that revenue conversion from deal wins can be uneven.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margin delivery and FY27 targets, with consistent messaging on discipline. Somewhat hedged on growth, citing macro uncertainty, client discretionary cuts and a need for more AI investment. Evasive on quantifying AI revenue.

key_quotes: We are reiterating our FY27 financial targets, sure you're happy to hear that, including achie ving organic constant currency revenue growth above our peer group's average and achieving an EBIT margin of 15%.
As we stand here today, there is confidence that growth will be certainly higher than it was in FY26, that a certain amount of growth is locked in
As we have delivered in the past, we remain very focused on working capital management and continue our emphasis to reduce receivables and improve the cash conversion over time.

As you can notice, we have not reported a number that you might have been expecting, which is around the revenue from AI, but I think as we progress over the next year we will start making sure that we start thinking about it differently.

growth.why: FY27 guidance is reiterated as above-peer-average organic cc growth (no numeric % given) and 15% EBIT margin, with FY27 growth expected to exceed FY26's +0.6% cc; delivery rests on AI-led fixed-price productivity (7% in programmes), a new token-based pricing model and record deal wins of USD 3.79B (+42%), but no capacity additions or firm order-book conversion numbers were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27, mainly H2 FY27 as fixed-price productivity ramps
rows.why: EBIT margin rose 290 bps to 12.6% in FY26 and Q4 margin was 13.8% (+70 bps QoQ); management reiterated 15% FY27 EBIT margin, with fixed-price vs T&M margin gap at about 8% and AI-led productivity at 7% in programmes.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity additions discussed; the company is an IT services firm and guidance centres on fresher hiring (900+ in FY26, a higher number planned for FY27) and tuck-in M&A, not plants or capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects FY27 growth to exceed FY26's +0.6% cc and be above peer average, backed by record FY26 deal wins of USD 3.79B (+42% YoY) and Q4 deal wins of USD 1,073M (+35% YoY), though large-deal revenue conversion has only reached 2.4% cc.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not a core discussion point; investment priority is shifting to AI (LLMs, platforms, people) rather than physical capacity, and the balance sheet holds USD 892M cash with FCF of USD 616M.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 targets were only reiterated (above-peer growth, 15% EBIT) with no numeric revenue guide; management is hedged on growth citing client discretionary cuts and macro uncertainty.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth is hedged on discretionary client cuts, telecom concentration and healthcare/hi-tech weakness, with large-deal revenue conversion uneven (-1% to 2.4% cc over four quarters).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is moving to an AI-native token-based pricing model and cites Orion (agent orchestration) and Helix as platforms in the market, though no launch dates were given.

rows.label: Token-based AI-native pricing model
rows.why: Management is moving toward a service-token pricing model blending human and digital labour, while clients push for higher outer-year productivity pass-through (AI productivity at 7% in programmes).

rows.label: Record FY26 deal wins
rows.why: FY26 deal wins reached USD 3.79B (+42% YoY) with Q4 at USD 1,073M (+35% YoY), and large-deal signings were not delayed despite Claude releases, but revenue conversion has been uneven.

rows.label: Tuck-in acquisitions and back-end integration
rows.why: Management will look at tuck-in acquisitions for capability rather than large M&A, and expects four to five back-end portfolio integrations to complete in FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin delivery (15% FY27 EBIT target, fixed-price productivity) and deal momentum, but cautious on growth given client discretionary cuts and telecom concentration, and evasive on quantifying AI revenue; analysts pushed on FY27 outperformance versus peers, telecom mega-d
